title: Financial Data Transparency Act Joint Data Standards
abstract: The OCC, Board, FDIC, NCUA, CFPB, FHFA, CFTC, SEC, and Treasury are publishing a final joint rule to establish data standards to promote interoperability of financial regulatory data across these agencies. The standards established pursuant to this joint rule will later be considered for potential incorporation (to the extent feasible) into data standards to be adopted for certain collections of information in separate rulemakings by the agencies or through other actions taken by the agencies. At the effective date, the joint rule will not change any reporting requirements without further action by the agencies. The agencies are publishing this joint rule as required by the Financial Data Transparency Act of 2022.
judge_reasoning: None of the retrieved excerpts address financial regulatory reporting data standards or the Financial Data Transparency Act, focusing instead on consumer data privacy, cybersecurity, and product compliance.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
abstract: The Securities and Exchange Commission ("Commission") is adopting amendments to Volumes I and II of the Electronic Data Gathering, Analysis, and Retrieval system Filer Manual ("EDGAR Filer Manual" or "Filer Manual") and related rules and forms. EDGAR Release 26.1 was deployed in the EDGAR system on March 16, 2026.

title: Application of the Federal Securities Laws to Certain Types of Crypto Assets and Certain Transactions Involving Crypto Assets
abstract: The Securities and Exchange Commission ("Commission" or "SEC") issues herein an interpretation regarding the application of the Federal securities laws to certain types of crypto assets and certain transactions involving crypto assets. The references in this release to "we" and "our" are to the Commission. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission ("CFTC") provides herein guidance relating to that interpretation.

title: Holding Foreign Insiders Accountable Act Disclosure
abstract: The Securities and Exchange Commission ("Commission") is adopting final amendments to certain of its rules and forms under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 ("Exchange Act") to reflect the requirements of the Holding Foreign Insiders Accountable Act ("HFIA Act"). The HFIA Act amended Section 16(a) of the Exchange Act to require directors and officers of a foreign private issuer with a class of equity securities registered under Section 12 of the Exchange Act to provide disclosure of their beneficial ownership and transactions involving the issuer's equity securities. The final amendments revise the Commission's rules and forms to reflect these statutory requirements.
judge_reasoning: None of the retrieved chunks discuss insider beneficial ownership disclosures, Section 16(a) of the Exchange Act, or regulations targeting foreign private issuers.

title: Acceleration of Effectiveness of Registration Statements of Issuers With Certain Mandatory Arbitration Provisions
abstract: The Securities and Exchange Commission ("Commission") is issuing this statement to inform the public that the presence of a provision requiring arbitration of investor claims arising under the Federal securities laws will not impact decisions regarding whether to accelerate the effectiveness of a registration statement. Accordingly, when making such decisions, the staff will focus on the adequacy of the registration statement's disclosures, including disclosure regarding the arbitration provision.
judge_reasoning: None of the retrieved chunks discuss SEC registration statements, mandatory arbitration provisions for investor claims, or the acceleration of registration statements.

title: Adjusting Imports of Semiconductors, Semiconductor Manufacturing Equipment, and Their Derivative Products Into the United States
abstract: Presidential Proclamation 11002, issued under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, following a Commerce Department investigation finding that import levels of semiconductors, semiconductor manufacturing equipment, and their derivative products threaten to impair U.S. national security. The proclamation imposes a 25 percent ad valorem tariff on a defined set of covered semiconductor products, effective January 15, 2026, with exceptions for imports that support the buildout of U.S. domestic semiconductor manufacturing capacity.
judge_reasoning: Chunk 1 is directly relevant because it discusses the pending Section 232 investigation into imports of semiconductors and their derivative products, which has now culminated in the newly issued Presidential Proclamation 11002.

title: Registered Offering Reform
abstract: [Claude-paraphrased, not official API metadata] Proposed rule from the Securities and Exchange Commission intended to facilitate capital formation in the public securities markets by significantly expanding Form S-3 shelf-registration eligibility, extending enhanced registration and communication benefits historically reserved for well-known seasoned issuers to a broader set of listed companies, modernizing Form S-1 incorporation-by-reference, and preempting state blue-sky registration requirements for registered offerings.

title: Heightened Import Disclosures for Supply Chain Visibility
abstract: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is considering amending its regulations to give CBP greater visibility into the supply chains of goods imported into the United States. CBP is seeking comments on new requirements enhancing visibility into the parties involved in the importation of goods; integrating innovative technical solutions for the tracing of supply chains of those goods; and collecting foreign export documentation that foreign exporters are required to submit to the foreign customs authority prior to the exportation of those goods to the United States. With these proposals, CBP seeks to more effectively detect and interdict illicit importations, especially those that are illegally transshipped to evade compliance with U.S. customs and trade laws.
judge_reasoning: Chunk 3 is substantively relevant because it addresses the risk of changing import and export regulations and the potential for products to be banned or delayed from importation due to compliance failures, which directly aligns with the proposed CBP supply chain visibility and disclosure requirements.

title: Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule
abstract: The Federal Trade Commission amends the Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule (the "Rule"), consistent with the requirements of the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act. The amendments to the Rule, which are based on the FTC's review of public comments and its enforcement experience, include one new definition and modifications to several others, as well as updates to key provisions to respond to changes in technology and online practices. The amendments are intended to strengthen protection of personal information collected from children, and, where appropriate, to clarify and streamline the Rule since it was last amended in January 2013.
